sanskrit: nighnanto niśitaiḥ śastrair bhrātṝn putrān sakhīn api yodhāḥ paripatanti sma yathāmiṣakṛte khagāḥ
english: Striking down brothers, sons, and even friends with their sharpened weapons, the warriors fell upon one another like birds contending over a scrap of flesh.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ pratisaṃrabdhāḥ samāsādya parasparam ahaṃ pūrvam ahaṃ pūrvam iti nyaghnan sahasraśaḥ
english: Enraged against each other, closing in man to man, crying "I first! I first!" they slew by the thousand.

sanskrit: saṃghātair āsanabhraṣṭair aśvārohair gatāsubhiḥ hayāḥ paripatanti sma śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: With their riders flung from the saddle and lifeless, the horses too fell in heaps by the hundred and by the thousand.

sanskrit: sphuratāṃ pratipiṣṭānām aśvānāṃ śīghrasāriṇām stanatāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ saṃnaddhānāṃ viśāṃ pate
english: From the swift-coursing horses, twitching and crushed, and from the armored men groaning aloud, O lord of peoples,

sanskrit: śaktyṛṣṭiprāsaśabdaś ca tumulaḥ samajāyata bhindatāṃ paramarmāṇi rājan durmantrite tava
english: there arose a tumultuous din of lances, swords, and javelins, as they pierced one another's vital points—O king, the fruit of your evil counsel.

sanskrit: śramābhibhūtāḥ saṃrabdhāḥ śrāntavāhāḥ pipāsitāḥ vikṣatāś ca śitaiḥ śastrair abhyavartanta tāvakāḥ
english: Overcome by exhaustion, frenzied, their mounts worn out, parched with thirst, and torn by sharpened weapons, your men yet pressed on into battle.

sanskrit: mattā rudhiragandhena bahavo 'tra vicetasaḥ jaghnuḥ parān svakāṃś caiva prāptān prāptān anantarān
english: Maddened by the smell of blood, many here lost their senses and struck down foe and kinsman alike, whoever came next within reach.

sanskrit: bahavaś ca gataprāṇāḥ kṣatriyā jayagṛddhinaḥ bhūmāv abhyapatan rājañ śaravṛṣṭibhir āvṛtāḥ
english: And many warriors, greedy for victory, their lives gone out, fell to the earth, O king, enveloped in showers of arrows.

sanskrit: vṛkagṛdhraśṛgālānāṃ tumule modane 'hani āsīd balakṣayo ghoras tava putrasya paśyataḥ
english: On that day of riotous feasting for wolves, vultures, and jackals, a fearful destruction of the host came to pass before your son's very eyes.

sanskrit: narāśvakāyasaṃchannā bhūmir āsīd viśāṃ pate rudhirodakacitrā ca bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhinī
english: The ground, O lord of peoples, lay strewn with the bodies of men and horses and dappled with streams of blood, deepening the dread of the faint-hearted.

sanskrit: asibhiḥ paṭṭiśaiḥ śūlais takṣamāṇāḥ punaḥ punaḥ tāvakāḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva nābhyavartanta bhārata
english: Hewn again and again by swords, pikes, and spears, neither your men nor the Pāṇḍavas turned back, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: praharanto yathāśakti yāvat prāṇasya dhāraṇam yodhāḥ paripatanti sma vamanto rudhiraṃ vraṇaiḥ
english: Striking with all their might so long as breath held within them, the warriors fell, vomiting blood from their wounds.

sanskrit: śiro gṛhītvā keśeṣu kabandhaḥ samadṛśyata udyamya niśitaṃ khaḍgaṃ rudhireṇa samukṣitam
english: A headless trunk was seen, gripping a head by its hair and raising a keen sword drenched in blood.

sanskrit: athotthiteṣu bahuṣu kabandheṣu janādhipa tathā rudhiragandhena yodhāḥ kaśmalam āviśan
english: And as many headless trunks rose up, O ruler of men, and from the reek of blood, the warriors sank into a swoon.

sanskrit: mandībhūte tataḥ śabde pāṇḍavānāṃ mahad balam alpāvaśiṣṭais turagair abhyavartata saubalaḥ
english: Then, as the clamor died down, Saubala, with the few horses that remained to him, advanced against the great host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyadhāvaṃs tvaritāḥ pāṇḍavā jayagṛddhinaḥ padātayaś ca nāgāś ca sādinaś codyatāyudhāḥ
english: Thereupon the Pāṇḍavas, greedy for victory, rushed swiftly upon him—footmen and elephants and horsemen with weapons upraised.

sanskrit: koṣṭakīkṛtya cāpy enaṃ parikṣipya ca sarvaśaḥ śastrair nānāvidhair jaghnur yuddhapāraṃ titīrṣavaḥ
english: Hemming him in within an enclosure and surrounding him on every side, they struck at him with weapons of every kind, eager to reach the farther shore of the war.

sanskrit: tvadīyās tāṃs tu saṃprekṣya sarvataḥ samabhidrutān sāśvapattidviparathāḥ pāṇḍavān abhidudruvuḥ
english: But your men, seeing them charging in from every quarter, rushed against the Pāṇḍavas with horse, foot, elephants, and chariots.

sanskrit: ke cit padātayaḥ padbhir muṣṭibhiś ca parasparam nijaghnuḥ samare śūrāḥ kṣīṇaśastrās tato 'patan
english: Some footmen, brave men with their weapons spent, struck at one another in the fray with feet and fists, and so fell.

sanskrit: rathebhyo rathinaḥ petur dvipebhyo hastisādinaḥ vimānebhya iva bhraṣṭāḥ siddhāḥ puṇyakṣayād yathā
english: Charioteers fell from their chariots and elephant-riders from their elephants, like Siddhas cast down from their celestial cars when their merit is exhausted.

sanskrit: evam anyonyam āyastā yodhā jaghnur mahāmṛdhe pitṝn bhrātṝn vayasyāṃś ca putrān api tathāpare
english: Thus, straining against one another in the great battle, the warriors slew—fathers, brothers, comrades, and others their very sons.

sanskrit: evam āsīd amaryādaṃ yuddhaṃ bharatasattama prāsāsibāṇakalile vartamāne sudāruṇe
english: So lawless was that battle, O best of the Bhāratas, as the dreadful welter of javelins, swords, and arrows raged on.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasmiñ śabde mṛdau jāte pāṇḍavair nihate bale aśvaiḥ saptaśataiḥ śiṣṭair upāvartata saubalaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When the clamor had grown faint and the host lay slaughtered by the Pāṇḍavas, Saubala turned about with the seven hundred horses that remained.

sanskrit: sa yātvā vāhinīṃ tūrṇam abravīt tvarayan yudhi yudhyadhvam iti saṃhṛṣṭāḥ punaḥ punar ariṃdamaḥ apṛcchat kṣatriyāṃs tatra kva nu rājā mahārathaḥ
english: Riding swiftly to the army, that tamer of foes urged it on, crying again and again to the joyous men, "Fight on!"—and he asked the warriors there, "Where now is the king, the great chariot-hero?"

sanskrit: śakunes tu vacaḥ śrutvā ta ūcur bharatarṣabha asau tiṣṭhati kauravyo raṇamadhye mahārathaḥ
english: Hearing Śakuni's words, they answered, O bull of the Bhāratas: "Yonder stands the Kaurava, the great chariot-hero, in the midst of the battle—

sanskrit: yatraitat sumahac chatraṃ pūrṇacandrasamaprabham yatraite satalatrāṇā rathās tiṣṭhanti daṃśitāḥ
english: there where that vast parasol shines bright as the full moon, where these armored chariots stand with their guards and finger-shields ready.

sanskrit: yatraiṣa śabdas tumulaḥ parjanyaninadopamaḥ tatra gaccha drutaṃ rājaṃs tato drakṣyasi kauravam
english: Where this tumultuous roar resounds like the thundering of a storm-cloud, go thither swiftly, O king, and there you shall behold the Kaurava."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu taiḥ śūraiḥ śakuniḥ saubalas tadā prayayau tatra yatrāsau putras tava narādhipa sarvataḥ saṃvṛto vīraiḥ samareṣv anivartibhiḥ
english: Thus addressed by those brave men, Śakuni Saubala then set forth to where your son stood, O ruler of men, encircled on all sides by heroes who never turned back in battle.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaṃ dṛṣṭvā rathānīke vyavasthitam sarathāṃs tāvakān sarvān harṣayañ śakunis tataḥ
english: Then, beholding Duryodhana stationed amid the array of chariots, Śakuni heartened all your chariot-warriors,

sanskrit: duryodhanam idaṃ vākyaṃ hṛṣṭarūpo viśāṃ pate kṛtakāryam ivātmānaṃ manyamāno 'bravīn nṛpam
english: and with a joyful air, O lord of peoples, deeming his task all but accomplished, spoke this word to King Duryodhana:

sanskrit: jahi rājan rathānīkam aśvāḥ sarve jitā mayā nātyaktvā jīvitaṃ saṃkhye śakyo jetuṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: "Slay the chariot-host, O king! All the horsemen have been vanquished by me. Yet Yudhiṣṭhira cannot be conquered in battle without staking one's very life.

sanskrit: hate tasmin rathānīke pāṇḍavenābhipālite gajān etān haniṣyāmaḥ padātīṃś cetarāṃs tathā
english: When that chariot-host guarded by the Pāṇḍava is destroyed, we shall slay these elephants and the footmen and the rest as well."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya tāvakā jayagṛddhinaḥ javenābhyapatan hṛṣṭāḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm
english: Hearing his words, your men, greedy for victory, fell joyfully and at speed upon the army of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: sarve vivṛtatūṇīrāḥ pragṛhītaśarāsanāḥ śarāsanāni dhunvānāḥ siṃhanādaṃ pracakrire
english: All with quivers thrown open and bows seized fast, brandishing their bows, they raised a lion's roar.

sanskrit: tato jyātalanirghoṣaḥ punar āsīd viśāṃ pate prādurāsīc charāṇāṃ ca sumuktānāṃ sudāruṇaḥ
english: Then once more, O lord of peoples, arose the din of bowstrings and palm-guards, and a most terrible noise of well-loosed arrows.

sanskrit: tān samīpagatān dṛṣṭvā javenodyatakārmukān uvāca devakīputraṃ kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Seeing them drawn near at speed with bows upraised, Dhanaṃjaya, the son of Kuntī, said to the son of Devakī:

sanskrit: codayāśvān asaṃbhrāntaḥ praviśaitad balārṇavam antam adya gamiṣyāmi śatrūṇāṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: "Urge on the horses without fear and plunge into this ocean of armies. Today I shall make an end of my enemies with sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: aṣṭādaśa dināny adya yuddhasyāsya janārdana vartamānasya mahataḥ samāsādya parasparam
english: Eighteen days, O Janārdana, has this great war now lasted, as the hosts have closed against each other.

sanskrit: anantakalpā dhvajinī bhūtvā hy eṣāṃ mahātmanām kṣayam adya gatā yuddhe paśya daivaṃ yathāvidham
english: The banner-host of these great-souled men, once seeming endless, has come to destruction in the battle this day—behold how fate works its will!

sanskrit: samudrakalpaṃ tu balaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya mādhava asmān āsādya saṃjātaṃ goṣpadopamam acyuta
english: The army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, vast as the sea, O Mādhava, on meeting us has become like the print of a cow's hoof, O undecaying one.

sanskrit: hate bhīṣme ca saṃdadhyāc chivaṃ syād iha mādhava na ca tat kṛtavān mūḍho dhārtarāṣṭraḥ subāliśaḥ
english: Had he made peace when Bhīṣma fell, well would it have been, O Mādhava; but that fool, the witless son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, did not do so.

sanskrit: uktaṃ bhīṣmeṇa yad vākyaṃ hitaṃ pathyaṃ ca mādhava tac cāpi nāsau kṛtavān vītabuddhiḥ suyodhanaḥ
english: The word that Bhīṣma spoke, salutary and wholesome, O Mādhava, that too senseless Suyodhana did not heed.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu patite bhīṣme pracyute pṛthivītale na jāne kāraṇaṃ kiṃ nu yena yuddham avartata
english: When Bhīṣma had fallen, struck down upon the face of the earth, I know not what cause it was for which the war went on.

sanskrit: mūḍhāṃs tu sarvathā manye dhārtarāṣṭrān subāliśān patite śaṃtanoḥ putre ye 'kārṣuḥ saṃyugaṃ punaḥ
english: Wholly deluded and utterly foolish I deem the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who, when the son of Śaṃtanu had fallen, yet renewed the battle.

sanskrit: anantaraṃ ca nihate droṇe brahmavidāṃ vare rādheye ca vikarṇe ca naivāśāmyata vaiśasam
english: And thereafter, when Droṇa, best of those versed in the Veda, was slain, and Rādheya and Vikarṇa, still the slaughter did not cease.

sanskrit: alpāvaśiṣṭe sainye 'smin sūtaputre ca pātite saputre vai naravyāghre naivāśāmyata vaiśasam
english: When this army had but little left, and the son of the charioteer, that tiger among men, was struck down together with his son, still the slaughter did not cease.

sanskrit: śrutāyuṣi hate śūre jalasaṃdhe ca paurave śrutāyudhe ca nṛpatau naivāśāmyata vaiśasam
english: When the hero Śrutāyus was slain, and Jalasaṃdha of the Pauravas, and King Śrutāyudha, still the slaughter did not cease.

sanskrit: bhūriśravasi śalye ca śālve caiva janārdana āvantyeṣu ca vīreṣu naivāśāmyata vaiśasam
english: When Bhūriśravas and Śalya and Śālva too, O Janārdana, and the heroes of the Avantis fell, still the slaughter did not cease.

sanskrit: jayadrathe ca nihate rākṣase cāpy alāyudhe bāhlike somadatte ca naivāśāmyata vaiśasam
english: When Jayadratha was slain, and the rākṣasa Alāyudha, and Bāhlika and Somadatta, still the slaughter did not cease.

sanskrit: bhagadatte hate śūre kāmboje ca sudakṣiṇe duḥśāsane ca nihate naivāśāmyata vaiśasam
english: When the brave Bhagadatta was slain, and Sudakṣiṇa of the Kāmbojas, and Duḥśāsana laid low, still the slaughter did not cease.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca nihatāñ śūrān pṛthaṅ māṇḍalikān nṛpān balinaś ca raṇe kṛṣṇa naivāśāmyata vaiśasam
english: And though he saw brave warriors slain, the kings of many provinces one by one, and the mighty fallen in battle, O Kṛṣṇa, still the slaughter did not cease.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇīpatīn dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenena pātitān mohād vā yadi vā lobhān naivāśāmyata vaiśasam
english: Seeing the commanders of whole armies struck down by Bhīmasena, whether from delusion or from greed, still the slaughter did not cease.

sanskrit: ko nu rājakule jātaḥ kauraveyo viśeṣataḥ nirarthakaṃ mahad vairaṃ kuryād anyaḥ suyodhanāt
english: What other man born in a royal house, a Kaurava above all, would wage so great and so fruitless a feud, save Suyodhana?

sanskrit: guṇato 'bhyadhikaṃ jñātvā balataḥ śauryato 'pi vā amūḍhaḥ ko nu yudhyeta jānan prājño hitāhitam
english: Knowing his foe the greater in worth, in strength, and in valor, what man not deluded, what wise man who discerns his good from his harm, would still make war?

sanskrit: yan na tasya mano hy āsīt tvayoktasya hitaṃ vacaḥ praśame pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ so 'nyasya śṛṇuyāt katham
english: Since his mind would not bend even when you spoke the salutary word of peace with the Pāṇḍavas, how should he hearken to any other?

sanskrit: yena śāṃtanavo bhīṣmo droṇo vidura eva ca pratyākhyātāḥ śamasyārthe kiṃ nu tasyādya bheṣajam
english: He by whom Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu, and Droṇa, and Vidura too were rebuffed when they pleaded for peace—what cure is there for him today?

sanskrit: maurkhyād yena pitā vṛddhaḥ pratyākhyāto janārdana tathā mātā hitaṃ vākyaṃ bhāṣamāṇā hitaiṣiṇī pratyākhyātā hy asatkṛtya sa kasmai rocayed vacaḥ
english: He who in his folly, O Janārdana, spurned his aged father, and who slighted and rejected his mother as she spoke the salutary word out of love for his welfare—to whose counsel would such a man ever incline?

sanskrit: kulāntakaraṇo vyaktaṃ jāta eṣa janārdana tathāsya dṛśyate ceṣṭā nītiś caiva viśāṃ pate naiṣa dāsyati no rājyam iti me matir acyuta
english: Plainly this man was born to be the ruin of his line, O Janārdana; so do his conduct and his policy appear, O lord of peoples. He will never yield us our kingdom—such is my conviction, O undecaying one.

sanskrit: ukto 'haṃ bahuśas tāta vidureṇa mahātmanā na jīvan dāsyate bhāgaṃ dhārtarāṣṭraḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Many a time, my friend, the great-souled Vidura told me: while he lives, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will in no wise grant you your portion.

sanskrit: yāvat prāṇā dhamiṣyanti dhārtarāṣṭrasya mānada tāvad yuṣmāsv apāpeṣu pracariṣyati pātakam
english: "So long as breath stirs within the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O giver of honor, so long will he work his wickedness against you who are sinless."

sanskrit: na sa yukto 'nyathā jetum ṛte yuddhena mādhava ity abravīt sadā māṃ hi viduraḥ satyadarśanaḥ
english: "He cannot be overcome by any means save war," O Mādhava—thus Vidura, the seer of truth, said to me ever again.

sanskrit: tat sarvam adya jānāmi vyavasāyaṃ durātmanaḥ yad uktaṃ vacanaṃ tena vidureṇa mahātmanā
english: All that resolve of the wicked one I now perceive this day to be true, even as it was spoken by the great-souled Vidura.

sanskrit: yo hi śrutvā vacaḥ pathyaṃ jāmadagnyād yathātatham avāmanyata durbuddhir dhruvaṃ nāśamukhe sthitaḥ
english: For that fool who, having heard the wholesome and faithful counsel of the son of Jamadagni, made light of it, stands surely at the threshold of his ruin.

sanskrit: uktaṃ hi bahubhiḥ siddhair jātamātre suyodhane enaṃ prāpya durātmānaṃ kṣayaṃ kṣatraṃ gamiṣyati
english: For it was foretold by many Siddhas at the very birth of Suyodhana: "On this wicked one's coming, the warrior race shall go to its destruction."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ vacanaṃ teṣāṃ niruktaṃ vai janārdana kṣayaṃ yātā hi rājāno duryodhanakṛte bhṛśam
english: And that word of theirs has now come true, O Janārdana, for kings in multitudes have gone to their destruction for Duryodhana's sake.

sanskrit: so 'dya sarvān raṇe yodhān nihaniṣyāmi mādhava kṣatriyeṣu hateṣv āśu śūnye ca śibire kṛte
english: This day, O Mādhava, I shall slay all his warriors in battle; and when the warriors are swiftly slain and his camp left empty,

sanskrit: vadhāya cātmano 'smābhiḥ saṃyugaṃ rocayiṣyati tad antaṃ hi bhaved vairam anumānena mādhava
english: he will choose, to his own undoing, to do battle with us; and so, by my reckoning, this feud shall come to its end, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: evaṃ paśyāmi vārṣṇeya cintayan prajñayā svayā vidurasya ca vākyena ceṣṭayā ca durātmanaḥ
english: Thus do I see it, O Vārṣṇeya, reflecting with my own understanding, by the word of Vidura and by the conduct of that wicked one.

sanskrit: saṃyāhi bhāratīṃ vīra yāvad dhanmi śitaiḥ śaraiḥ duryodhanaṃ durātmānaṃ vāhinīṃ cāsya saṃyuge
english: Drive on into the Bhārata host, O hero, that I may slay with sharpened arrows the wicked Duryodhana and his army in the fray.

sanskrit: kṣemam adya kariṣyāmi dharmarājasya mādhava hatvaitad durbalaṃ sainyaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya paśyataḥ
english: This day I shall secure the welfare of the Dharma King, O Mādhava, by destroying this feeble army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son before his very eyes."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca abhīśuhasto dāśārhas tathoktaḥ savyasācinā tad balaugham amitrāṇām abhītaḥ prāviśad raṇe
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus addressed by Savyasācin, the Dāśārha, reins in hand, fearlessly entered amid the flood of the enemy's host in battle.

sanskrit: śarāsanavaraṃ ghoraṃ śaktikaṇṭakasaṃvṛtam gadāparighapanthānaṃ rathanāgamahādrumam
english: That dreadful army—where the choicest bows were thorny thickets bristling with lances, its pathways maces and iron clubs, its great trees the chariots and elephants—

sanskrit: hayapattilatākīrṇaṃ gāhamāno mahāyaśāḥ vyacarat tatra govindo rathenātipatākinā
english: strewn over with creepers of horse and foot—Govinda of great renown, plunging into it, ranged through it there on his banner-decked chariot.

sanskrit: te hayāḥ pāṇḍurā rājan vahanto 'rjunam āhave dikṣu sarvāsv adṛśyanta dāśārheṇa pracoditāḥ
english: Those white horses, O king, bearing Arjuna into battle and urged on by the Dāśārha, were seen ranging in all directions.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāyād rathenājau savyasācī paraṃtapaḥ kirañ śaraśatāṃs tīkṣṇān vāridhārā ivāmbudaḥ
english: Then Savyasācin, scorcher of foes, advanced on his chariot into the fight, scattering keen arrows by the hundred like a cloud pouring down its torrents of rain.

sanskrit: prādurāsīn mahāñ śabdaḥ śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām iṣubhiś chādyamānānāṃ samare savyasācinā
english: A great noise arose from the smooth-jointed arrows as the field was covered over with shafts by Savyasācin.

sanskrit: asajjantas tanutreṣu śaraughāḥ prāpatan bhuvi indrāśanisamasparśā gāṇḍīvapreṣitāḥ śarāḥ
english: Without lodging in the armor, the floods of arrows fell to the ground—shafts loosed from the Gāṇḍīva, whose touch was like the thunderbolt of Indra.

sanskrit: narān nāgān samāhatya hayāṃś cāpi viśāṃ pate apatanta raṇe bāṇāḥ pataṃgā iva ghoṣiṇaḥ
english: Striking down men, elephants, and horses too, O lord of peoples, the arrows fell upon the field like swarms of humming locusts.

sanskrit: āsīt sarvam avacchannaṃ gāṇḍīvapreṣitaiḥ śaraiḥ na prājñāyanta samare diśo vā pradiśo 'pi vā
english: All was overspread with the shafts loosed from the Gāṇḍīva, and in the battle neither the quarters nor the intermediate quarters could be discerned.

sanskrit: sarvam āsīj jagat pūrṇaṃ pārthanāmāṅkitaiḥ śaraiḥ rukmapuṅkhais tailadhautaiḥ karmāraparimārjitaiḥ
english: The whole world seemed filled with arrows graven with Pārtha's name—gold-feathered, washed in oil, and burnished by the smith.
